coptic_restorations.basis: Single-letter completion of ⲯⲩⲭⲏ at line edge; the standard Greek loanword for 'soul' continues onto the next line where ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'living' modifies it.
Completes ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'living', forming the standard Manichaean phrase ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'the living soul' (cf. l.62 ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ within the same teaching).
Completes ⲁⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'to go upward', the standard Manichaean idiom of ascent toward the homeland (paralleled in numerous Kephalaia ascent passages).
Completes ⲥⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ ⲛ̄ⲥⲣ̄ⲁⲓⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ 'she knows and-she-perceives'; standard verbal coordination, picking up after line-edge ⲥⲥⲁⲩ in the prior segment.

The relative clause ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲉϩⲗⲱⲭⲥ̄ ⲉⲧ-{verb}-ⲙⲙⲁⲥ requires the cognate verb stem of the agent-noun ⲣⲉϩⲗⲱⲭⲥ̄ 'defiler' (Lycopolitan equivalent of ⲗⲱⲃϣ). The verb stem ⲗⲱⲭⲥ̄ 'defile' fits the est. 3-character span (overstroke not counted) and matches the agent-noun morphology already present.
Single-letter restoration of ⲉⲙⲏⲧⲓ 'except', parallel to ⲉⲓⲙⲏⲧⲓ in line 59 of the same teaching.

After ⲛⲉ closing the prior clause ('they are [the luminaries of the heavens]'), a coordinating connective is needed to introduce the new clause ⲥⲉϣⲱⲡⲉ ⲛⲉⲥ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲛⲙⲧⲁⲛ. ⲁⲩⲱ 'and' is the standard Lycopolitan conjunction at exactly 3 characters; matches the rhythm of parallel passages.
ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'in the going-forth' supplies the spatial-modal phrase governing the gate-imagery of departure.
Completes ⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the house of her men', the formula already seen in line 51 (ⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ) and l.64.
Completes ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'the land of light' (lexicon: ⲡⲕⲁϩ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ, the inmost state where the Lord dwells); reappears in l.65 as ⲡⲧⲕⲁⲍ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈[ⲛⲉ].
Genitive linker ⲛ̄ before ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ, completing the formula ⲁⲧⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'unto the house of her men' (cf. ll.51, 57, 64).
Completes ⲛ̄ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ 'of the heavens' (cf. l.55, l.58 ⲙⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ ⲛ̄ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ).
Completes ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'forever', the standard doxological terminus continuing into l.68 ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ.

english_restorations.basis: ⲯⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ = 'living soul'; lexicon entry ⲧⲩⲭⲏ 'soul/psyche' as the rational and its life. The Coptic ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ from the next segment is folded into 'living' here for natural English flow; the placeholder marks 'soul' specifically.
ⲁⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ = 'to go upward', the lexicon's ascent action (ⲉⲓ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ family); the soul's elevation toward the Lord.

Completes the verbal coordination ⲥⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ ⲛ̄ⲥⲣ̄ⲁⲓⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ 'she knows and perceives'; the prior segment ended with 'But she' carrying the subject forward, so this picks up 'knows and' before the second verb 'perceives'.

Cognate verb to ⲣⲉϩⲗⲱⲭⲥ̄ 'defilers' just preceding; the relative clause says they are her defilers 'who defile her in every place'. Lexicon: ⲗⲱⲃϣ family — defilement of the soul by the natural states it has claimed.
Coordinating connective ⲁⲩⲱ 'and' linking 'they are [the luminaries]' with the new clause 'they become for her a place of rest'.
ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'in the going-forth' — the spatial-modal phrase governing the open gate of departure.
ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'of her men' (the soul's own kindred); same formula recurs in lines 51, 63-64 of this teaching.
ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ = Land of Light (lexicon: ⲡⲕⲁϩ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ, the inmost state where the Lord dwells, the celestial degree of the regenerated rational).
Definite article ⲙ̄ in the genitive phrase ⲛ̄ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ 'of the heavens'; standard formula 'luminaries of the heavens' from lines 55, 58.
ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'forever' — 'for' here, with 'ever' continuing into the closing segment 4690; standard doxological terminus.

restoration_note: This teaching describes the living soul's ascent toward home: she finds that none of the powers of heaven and earth — the natural mind in any of its faculties — opens a gate for her, because they have been her defilers. Only the sun and moon (the Lord as illumining wisdom and as that wisdom received in the natural — Jesus the Radiance and Virgin of Light/the moon as receivable wisdom) become her place of rest and the open gate by which she passes out toward the country of her kindred. At the consummation, the Land of Light (the inmost dwelling of the Lord) becomes the final receiver of these luminaries themselves, and the soul reigns there with them forever. Most gaps were tightly constrained by formulaic repetition within the teaching itself: ⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ ('house of her men') recurs three times; ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ ⲛ̄ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ ('luminaries of the heavens') recurs four times; ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ ('land of light') frames the closing simile. The two genuine lacunae ({4} 'defile' and {6} 'and') were restored from immediate context (the cognate of ⲣⲉϩⲗⲱⲭⲥ̄, and the standard coordinating ⲁⲩⲱ); both at moderate confidence given fragmentary trace evidence. The remaining restorations are editor proposals confirmed by Manichaean idiom and lexicon vocabulary.
